note: CODE DERIVATION: data/shinohara_2021_testimony.py melts the S2 CSV's own column headers unchanged as item (allo_observation ... eva_neutral testimony; no rename, no positional assignment). The headers self-describe task (allo = reward-allocation, anti = reward-anticipation, eva = explicit evaluation) and puppet role (observation = puppet A, valence testimony = puppet B, neutral testimony = puppet C), mirroring the paper's Table 1 column heads 'First-hand observation / Testimony with valence / Neutral testimony'; S2 carries no label row, so the words come from the paper. RESP AXIS (inferred, then verified): allo/anti store the rank each puppet received, 1 = high reward (40 stickers) / first choice, 2 = medium (10 stickers) / second choice, 3 = low reward (one sticker) / least desired choice. This CONTRADICTS the processing script's header comment 'higher = larger reward given'; the data themselves are consistent with the paper (see verification). eva stores -2..2 exactly as the paper states (three x-marks -2 ... three stars 2). STRUCTURE: three real sections, one per task; item_text is the same for a puppet role across the three tasks. section_prompt and instructions are verbatim Methods sentences (reported speech from the paper, not a published experimenter script): allocation = 'They were asked to decide ... each box.'; anticipation = the paper's sentence verbatim including its 'high- reward-anticipation' spacing; evaluation = the first clause of the paper's sentence, cut before the scale-point list which is carried in option_text. item_text for the two testimony puppets quotes the paper's testimony wording verbatim for each condition/version (the neutral quote's missing closing quotation mark in the paper was supplied); item_text for puppet A is IRW's condensation of the paper's description of the wordless first-hand observation videos (positive: picked up the dropped ball/pencil; negative: destroyed the block castle or took the red ball). Each code covers several counterbalanced renderings (condition, video version, puppet colour, presentation order per S1 Table) - named, not picked. option_text: allocation = '40 stickers (high reward)' etc. verbatim from the paper; anticipation options lifted from the paper's sentence ('most wanted (high-reward-anticipation)', spacing typo normalised); evaluation = the paper's symbol plus label, e.g. 'three stars (very good)', with the paper's in-parenthesis numbers dropped because they are the resp value. LANGUAGE: the paper never names the administration language; Japanese is inferred from the sample (most from middle-class Japanese families in a small Japanese city), the NTT Communication Science Laboratories ethics approval and JSPS funding, and S1's Word styles being Japanese-locale. Recoverability checked: article HTML 0 CJK characters, S2 CSV 0, S1 DOCX visible text 0 (its 117 CJK characters are all Word style/font names in styles.xml/theme1.xml/fontTable.xml/app.xml). So fallback: English from the paper in base fields, language=Japanese, no _translated text. RIGHTS: the tasks and testimony scripts are this study's own paradigm, published by the authors in a CC BY 4.0 article; there is no separate instrument rights holder, no restriction clause located, no instrument_rights_register row, and none written. correct_response empty (attitude measures). Every item uses every resp level of its task (live table(item, resp): allo/anti 1-3 all populated, eva -2..2 all populated, e.g. eva_neutral testimony 2/1/29/50/46).
public_note: Item codes are puppet roles, not fixed puppets: which coloured puppet and which video version filled each role, and the presentation order, were counterbalanced, and the valence-testimony and first-hand-observation puppets were prosocial for the positive-condition half of the sample and antisocial for the negative-condition half (cov_condition); allocation and anticipation are stored as ranks where 1 is the highest reward or first choice and 3 the lowest, and the English prompts are the paper's descriptions of a procedure administered in Japanese rather than a published script

' item number from each label; (2) PHQ1's label is cut at SPSS's 255-character cap mid-word ('...Can't get motivated or uninterested in doin') -- completed as 'doing things', the ending of canonical PHQ-9 item 1 ('Little interest or pleasure in doing things'); the three added characters 'g things' are IRW's, not the file's; (3) trailing periods on two value labels ('A couple of days.' on PHQ1, 'Not at all.' on PHQ9) dropped, as the processing script also does; (4) item text otherwise verbatim, including the study's own non-canonical English (slashes in PHQ6/PHQ8, 'Can't get motivated...', 'reading the newspaper'). Its embedded anchor legend differs in wording from the value labels (For several days vs A couple of days; For more than a week vs More than half the time) -- two English renderings of the same Chinese options inside one file; option_text uses the value labels because they are what ties code to label, and the instruction legend is left literal. LANGUAGE / FALLBACK: sample is 1,190 secondary-school students in Changsha, China (Second Xiangya Hospital authors), so the administration was Chinese -- inferred from the sample, the paper does not name the questionnaire language. Recoverability scoped to deposit + supplements: the .sav (25 variables, every variable label and value label English, zero CJK characters across all of them), s002.doc (STROBE checklist only) and figures g001-g008 (model/response-surface plots); none carries Chinese wording. INSTRUMENT: the paper describes the 'eight-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-8)' plus a separate suicidal-ideation question 'Have you thought about dying or hurting yourself in any way in the past 2 weeks?' rated '1 (no) to 4 (almost every day)'. The deposit administers all nine as one block (question 52, items 1-9), PHQ9 is the self-harm item, stored 0-3 like the others, and the deposit's PHQtotal equals the 9-item sum for 1190/1190 respondents (8-item sum for 86%), so the table is correctly a PHQ-9; the paper's 1-4 coding of the suicide item is not how the file stores it. note: Clean pass with disclosed caveats. CODE DERIVATION: data/silva_2018_body_image.py melts the S1 xlsx columns starting 'MBDS' with names unchanged, so the item code IS the source column name; the numbers are the original 25-item MBDS (Ochner, Gray & Brickner 2009) item numbers, and the 12 present (1,2,4,6,8,9,12,15,16,19,21,23) are exactly the MBDS-R reduced form the PLOS paper says it used (Da Silva et al. 2017, ref 36). WORDING: neither the PLOS article nor its only supplement (S1 xlsx) prints any MBDS wording (labels sheet is generic). The PLOS paper names the administered version: 'The Portuguese version of the MBDS was presented by Carvalho et al. [35] and was the one used in this study', and the reduced form as Da Silva et al. [36]. Da Silva et al. 2017 (same group, Ochner co-author) Table 5 prints each reduced-form item by number in English and in Portuguese, footnoted 'MBDS English version was published by Ochner et al [29] and MBDS Portuguese version was published by Carvalho et al. [41]'. item_text = that Portuguese column verbatim (line-wrap joins only; curly double quotes kept as printed, checked on a 200-dpi render of p.524); item_text_translated = the English column verbatim. This is off-deposit but is the instrument version the study itself cites as administered, so it ships as the administered language rather than taking the translated_substitute fallback. The Carvalho et al. 2013 Cad Saude Publica original (doi:10.1590/S0102-311X2013000200027) was NOT retrieved (SciELO 403/504, UFJF repository no connection), so Table 5's Portuguese is a reprint and has not been diffed against it; instructions and the Likert/importance anchors were not recovered and are blank. Portugal's 373 respondents also received this Brazilian-Portuguese version per Da Silva 2017 ('the Portuguese version of the MBDS published by Carvalho et al.'). RESP: resp is NOT a selected option. Each item was answered twice (importance 1-10 and a 5-point agreement/frequency Likert) and the stored value is importance/10 x Likert (PLOS Methods; range .1-5.0). The 28 live resp values are exactly the 28 distinct products {i/10*j: i=1..10, j=1..5}; every item carries rows for all 28 (per-item use in the S1 source: 26-28 levels), option_text blank because no single option corresponds to a product. Direction: all 66 inter-item correlations in the S1 source are positive (min r=0.24), so the 12 items are co-keyed despite Table 5 marking 4,6,9,12,16 as reverse items; which direction the Likert runs was not recoverable from any retrieved source. RIGHTS: no stated restriction on MBDS wording located (web search for Ochner MBDS permission/copyright, nothing quotable); silence is permission. No register row written (a round may not write ship). VERIFICATION: route 1 against Da Silva 2017 Table 2 (BR/PT mean and SD for all 25 items), live data 429 BR + 373 PT: all 48 cells within 0.048; each item's nearest published 4-D profile is its own number among the 12 and also among all 25 (own distance 0.016-0.059 vs runner-up 0.129-0.623). verify_silva_2018_mbds.R -> VERDICT: PASS.
public_note: resp is not a chosen response option: each MBDS item was rated for importance (1-10) and on a 5-point agreement/frequency scale, and resp is importance/10 multiplied by that rating (0.1-5.0), so option_text is blank for all 28 observed values.

note: (1) CODE DERIVATION: pattern 1 -- the script melts S1 columns whose names start 'PHCS' with names kept, so PHCS1..PHCS8 ARE the deposit's column names. So the deposit ties no code to text. (2) MAPPING (paper_explicit): Silva et al. 2016 Table 1 -- the same group's validation paper that the 2018 paper cites as the administered unified Portuguese version -- numbers the items 1..8, and the codes carry the same numbers; the 2018 paper's reverse-item list (1,2,6,7) and bifactor item lists ({1,2,6,7},{3,4,5,8}) use that numbering. Checked (verify_silva_2018_phcs.R, VERDICT: PASS, status PARTIAL): polarity -- PHCS1/2/6/7 means 1.92/2.10/2.17/2.08 vs PHCS3/4/5/8 3.90/3.75/3.47/3.48, all 16 cross-block r negative (-0.54..-0.25); 2018 Table 1 PHCS-B loading ranges reproduced on the live data (women n=1396 published .54-.86 observed .54-.86; men n=802 .60-.83 vs .61-.83; women fitted with 3-4,4-5 residuals .54-.84 vs .55-.84; men fitted without items 1,3 .71-.85 vs .71-.85); of the 16 ways to drop one negative + one positive column for men, only PHCS1+PHCS3 reproduces .71-.85 (others .52-.87 ranges off); in women the within-positive MIs are 4-5 28.3, 3-4 26.0, 3-5 15.0, 4-8 10.9, 3-8 3.5, 5-8 3.2, so PHCS8 is in no pair above the papers' stated LM>11 criterion. An alternative ordering circulating in third-party reproductions (e.g. db.arabpsychology.com lists 'I handle myself well...' as item 1, reverse items 2,3,6,7) is refuted for THIS table by polarity: PHCS1 mean 1.92 and PHCS3 mean 3.90. All 8 items use all 5 levels (per-item counts from the S1 xlsx, e.g. PHCS1 979/659/373/141/46).
